primary_question: Does breeding-island architecture systematically alter local demographic coupling to shared species-wide forcing in Pygoscelis penguins?

primary_result.statistic: median gamma_AH across ADPE, CHPE, GEPE

secondary_breeding_space_H1.interpretation: directionally concordant but unsupported; cannot rescue the primary interaction

robustness.observation_timing: stable: exact-date and <=14-day offsets preserve all three negative gamma_AH signs and CHPE/GEPE crossover classification
robustness.spatial_scale: raw interaction estimates vary strongly across 1/2/5 km, but the joint sign-switch-plus-contrast null probability is 0.0810; treat this as radius sensitivity/instability, not established biological scale dependence
robustness.heterogeneity_metric: partly stable: 2 km Shannon preserves CHPE/GEPE crossover but not ADPE

allowed_claims: At the frozen 2 km Habitat Complex-richness scale, all three Pygoscelis species showed negative area-by-heterogeneity point estimates.
The preregistered cross-species permutation test did not confirm a general interaction at alpha=0.05.
Simple breeding-space buffering was also not supported by species-specific permutation tests.

Chinstrap and gentoo showed the full point-estimate option-fragmentation sign pattern at the primary 2 km richness scale, but these species-specific interactions did not survive Holm-adjusted permutation inference.
Breeding-island architecture therefore cannot currently be treated as a scale-invariant demographic filter of shared Antarctic forcing.

The interaction is sensitive to the spatial radius used to define breeding landscapes, but the observed 2-to-5 km sign reversal is compatible with the joint block-permutation null (plus-one probability 0.0810) and is not treated as established biological scale dependence.

The non-confirmatory primary result does not exclude moderate common interactions: retrospective detection was low near |gamma_AH|=0.30, whereas common effects around 0.50-0.55 would usually have been detected.
prohibited_claims: Island architecture buffers Antarctic penguin populations.
Habitat heterogeneity generally switches from fragmentation to insurance across Pygoscelis.
The option-fragmentation crossover is a general island-ecology law.
Adelie, chinstrap, and gentoo all show a confirmed crossover.
The 5 km or Shannon sensitivity may replace the frozen primary 2 km richness analysis.
Process variance or local demographic instability has an ecological interpretation; process-SD recovery remains blocked.
The 1/2/5 km sign reversal demonstrates biological scale dependence.
The primary null result establishes absence/equivalence of an area-by-heterogeneity effect.
paper_level_framing: A stringent test of reproductive-island buffering found directionally concordant but non-confirmatory effects. The study was sensitive to very large common interactions, while moderate interactions remained weakly detectable; apparent cross-radius sign reversal did not exceed the frozen joint null. Static breeding-island architecture therefore does not yield a confirmed transferable macroecological resilience rule.
paper1_link: Paper 1 documents within-island demographic reorganization. Paper 2 tests whether static breeding-island architecture predicts how that broader forcing is transmitted across colonies; the failure of a general predictor shows that local reorganization does not automatically scale into a transferable island-resilience rule.

retrospective_detectable_effect.interpretation: The design had low sensitivity to a common interaction around the observed magnitude but high sensitivity to very large common interactions around 0.50-0.55. This is not an equivalence bound.

radius_sign_switch_null.interpretation: The observed 2 km negative to 5 km positive reversal does not meet the frozen <=0.05 criterion for biological scale-dependence language.
